filler_material_original: s-BN (commercial h-BN self-modified with BN nanocrystals, BNNCs), polymer/s-BN composite film, 25 wt%
size_distribution: lateral size approximately 10–15 μm
functionalization: BNNC self-modified nanointerface: BN nanocrystals (~100 nm diameter, 1–4 nm thick, OH/NH groups) anchored on h-BN; 0.02 g BNNCs per 1 g h-BN
filler_alignment: lamellar BN at top and bottom surfaces with vertically connected BN chains inside (nano-CT)
processing_method: s-BN mixed into aqueous SA/PVA gel; gel dripped on substrate and pressed with Ca2+-containing monolith ice (ice-press assembly), solvent exchange in ethanol/acetone, dried at 60 °C; ~80 μm thick flexible film
measurement_method: Calculated from thermal diffusivity and specific heat capacity (Fig. S6); instrument not named in the main text
source_location: Results and Discussion, 'Thermal Performance of Polymer/s-BN Composite Films', paragraph 1: 'A point of inflection occurs at approximately 25 wt%, at which the through-plane thermal conductivity reaches the highest value of 21.3 W m−1 K−1, which is considerably higher than those of previously reported BN-based composites and more than twice the reported maximum (9.8 W m−1 K−1 at 50 wt% BN, Fig. 3b and Table S2) [28–40], at a simultaneously high in-plane thermal conductivity of 20.3 W m−1 K−1.'
notes: In-plane value of the 25 wt% polymer/s-BN film. Also stated in Introduction paragraph 3.

paper_title: Amino Acid-Assisted Sand-Milling Exfoliation of Boron Nitride Nanosheets for High Thermally Conductive Thermoplastic Polyurethane Composites
filler_material_original: pure TPU (neat matrix)
processing_method: Solution processed in DMF, precipitated in ethanol, dried; hot pressed at 180 °C (8 min unpressurized, then 10 MPa for 10 min)

filler_material_original: AlN + Al2O3 + 1 wt% pristine BNNT, sample PDMS/AlN/Al2O3/BNNT-neat
size_distribution: BNNT diameter 30–50 nm, length ~10 μm, purity >80% (remainder h-BN nanoparticles and nanoflakes); AlN and Al2O3 particle sizes not stated
processing_method: Sequential vortex mixing with a paste mixer: BNNT (if any) pre-blended with IPA and PDMS resin, solvent evaporated, Al2O3 and AlN added in order to 87% filler, then hardener/catalyst/retardant mixed in; poured into metal mold and hot-press cured at 120 °C for 2 h
measurement_method: Transient plane source, Hot Disk thermal analyzer TPS500S (isotropic thermal conductivity)
source_location: Section 3.2, paragraph 2: 'A certain amount of (1% wt.) BNNT-neat and BNNT-CAPA was then introduced into the composite system, and both composites demonstrated an improved thermal conductivity, with BNNT-neat obtaining 7.0 W/mK, while BNNT-CAPA attained 8.1 W/mK.'

AlN:Al2O3 split not stated. BNNT purity >80%, the remainder h-BN nanoparticles/nanoflakes. Corrected in verification: Value 7.0 is correct. The notes wrongly said it is not explicit whether the 1 wt% BNNT is inside the 87%; Section 2.3 implies it is (BNNT plus 'remaining filler' reach 87%).
